links.outcome: Hallucinated or invalid HPO terms in RAG-grounded LLM output, checked against official database
links.effect: 2,064 of 2,150 terms (96.0%) fully validated; hallucination rate 1.3%; HPO ID-name mismatch rate 2.7%. With GPT-5, no hallucinations on the new dataset.
links.quote: Across the 112 cases, a total of 2 150 HPO terms were generated; 2,064 (96.0%) were fully validated by the official database, with a hallucination rate of 1.3% and an HPO ID-name mismatch rate of 2.7%.

unlisted_practices: Using a retrieval-augmented LLM pipeline with official ontology database validation for phenotype term annotation
Comparing RAG-based annotation with dictionary tools and standalone LLMs

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks a new RAG-based pipeline/tool (PhenoRAG) for mapping clinical text to Human Phenotype Ontology terms on a retrospective dataset of case reports.
